important.name: _rel_path claims escape protection it does not enforce
important.summary:
The _rel_path docstring (config.py:481-485) says it repeats relPath 'so a load without jsonschema never accepts a path that escapes the project root'. The check rejects only a leading slash, a backslash or a drive letter, so '../shared/' passes, and so does the schema's relPath pattern. todo_inbox() then resolves outside the project. inbox put writes there, add --inbox deletes and renames files there, and default_exclusions writes a '../...' pattern. That breaks the plugin's 'data goes to the project' rule. The module already has _inside_root (config.py:517) for exactly this check.

Also (system_shape): config.py:480-489 `_rel_path` says it repeats the schema's relPath shape 'so a load without `jsonschema` never accepts a path that escapes the project root'. It rejects only a leading slash or backslash and a drive prefix. `../outside` and `docs/../../x` pass the check, and they pass the schema's relPath pattern as well. `todo_inbox()` (config.py:233-236) then points `inbox put` at a folder outside the project, and `history_paths` and the seeded exclusions take a pattern outside the repo. The mod mirror (config.ts `pathOr`, which skips `insideRoot`) would list that folder too. This contradicts the docstring and the project rule that drivers write only under the consuming project. The module already has `_inside_root` (config.py:517-521) for exactly this check on `todo.*` paths. The new tests (tests/lib/test_config_scratch_folder.py) cover only a non-string value.

Also (config): The `_rel_path` docstring says a load without jsonschema 'never accepts a path that escapes the project root', but the check (and the schema's relPath pattern in harness.schema.json line 38 via #/$defs/relPath) only rejects a leading slash, backslash or drive letter. A value such as `../outside` loads, and `todo_inbox()` then resolves the inbox (written by inbox.py `_write_items`) outside the project. The same file already has a `..` climb check for the todo paths (config.py ~518), so the contrast makes the claim misleading.

Also (overall): config.py:480-485 says the check 'never accepts a path that escapes the project root', but it rejects only a leading slash, backslash or drive letter. `scratch_folder: "../elsewhere"` passes both this check and the schema's relPath pattern (harness.schema.json:9). inbox put would then write queued items outside the project, and the todo-watch mod lists them from there.
fix: Normalize and bound the value: return _inside_root(posixpath.normpath(value.replace('\\', '/')), where) after the existing shape check (keep the original spelling when the trailing slash matters to todo_inbox).
Or drop the escape claim from the docstring, if a scratch folder above the root is intended.

In `_rel_path`, normalize (`posixpath.normpath(value.replace('\\', '/'))`) and pass the result through `_inside_root(..., where)`; apply `insideRoot` to `scratchFolder` in config.ts readConfig (falling back to the default); add a test that `scratch_folder: "../x"` raises ConfigError.
Or reword the `_rel_path` docstring so it claims only what it checks (no rooted or drive-prefixed path), and document in the README row that `..` is not refused.
Reword the `_rel_path` docstring to say it rejects absolute paths and drive letters only
Reject `..` climbing for scratch_folder with the existing climb helper near config.py:518, and add a schema note or test for it
Also reject any `..` segment in `_rel_path` (e.g. `'..' in PurePosixPath(value.replace('\\', '/')).parts`), and add a test case to tests/lib/test_config_scratch_folder.py.
Or narrow the docstring to what is checked: no leading slash, backslash or drive letter.

important.name: An accepted inbox file that cannot be deleted is drained again, duplicating a note item
important.summary:
drain writes the catalog first and only then deletes the accepted inbox files (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:286-288). When a delete fails (a Windows handle held on the file past the 5 x 50 ms retry, or the todo-watch 60 s DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS killing the child between write_edits and _remove_accepted), the file keeps its queued name, so queued() lists it again. The error only asks a person to delete it before the next drain, but todo-watch starts that next drain on its own at the next subagent turn end (drainQueued in plugins/todo-watch/hooks/checks.ts) or session start. A note item (no issue) is then added a second time under a fresh id; an issue item is refused as already in the catalog and set aside as .rejected.json, a spurious rejection.

Also (runtime): When _remove_accepted cannot delete a file whose items already landed, _problems (inbox.py:227-228) tells a person to delete it 'before the next drain'. The todo-watch mod starts a drain at every subagent turn end and session start while a queued *.json is listed (checks.ts drainQueued), so the next drain usually runs before anyone can act. A note item (no issue number for _check_spec to refuse) is then added a second time under a new id.

Attack: Pytest probe (ran at the PR head, passes, prints 'count 2'): with tests/lib/_todo_helpers.build(make_project), write docs/_scratch/todo-inbox/20261113T000001Z-00-aaaaaa.json holding {"items": [<a valid note item, no issue, title 'A local note'>]}; monkeypatch inbox._unlink_with_retry to raise PermissionError(13, 'file in use') and call inbox.drain(cfg) (raises TodoSyncError 'could not be deleted'); undo the patch and call inbox.drain(cfg) again (what the todo-watch turn-end trigger does next). The catalog now holds two items titled 'A local note' with different ids. Real-world trigger: on Windows, keep the inbox file open from another process (Python open() shares no delete) while 'todo_sync.py add --inbox' runs.
fix: Claim each queued file before the catalog write: rename it to a hidden name (for example '.<name>.draining', which queued() and isQueuedName already skip), absorb the claimed files, write the catalog, then delete the claimed files; on a failed catalog write rename them back. A file that cannot be claimed is skipped this drain instead of being added twice.
Record the drained inbox file names in a ledger under state_dir inside the same lock, and have queued() or _absorb skip a name the ledger already holds.
Rename an accepted file that cannot be deleted to a non-queued name (for example <stem>.added.json, skipped by queued() and isQueuedName), and retry the delete on a later drain.
Or record the accepted file names in state_dir and have queued() skip them until they are gone.

important.name: Notes about an unfreed lock or lease never reach the user
important.summary: locking._free_noting (locking.py:89-94) and catalog_lock.hold (catalog_lock.py:362-367) record a failed release with exc.add_note(...) so the original error is not replaced. main() prints only ' '.join(str(exc).split()), and str() of an exception leaves out __notes__. When `lease release` hits a recount, render or check failure and the free also fails, the user sees only the first error. The driver docstring says the lease is freed regardless, so the user assumes it is gone while it keeps blocking every writer, including the todo-watch drain, for up to 30 minutes. The same gap hides 'lock ... was not released' from a guarded write.
fix: In main(), add the exception's notes to the problem line: message = ' '.join(' '.join([str(exc), *getattr(exc, '__notes__', ())]).split()).
Or have _free_noting and hold raise a TodoSyncError/LockError whose message already names the release failure, in place of add_note.

important.name: Skills say a drain `problem:` line leaves the queued items in the inbox, but a drain can fail after the items landed
important.summary:
add-todo SKILL.md:85-86 and sync-gh-todo SKILL.md:75-76 tell the main session: 'A `problem:` line ends the run: relay it once without rerunning the drain; the queued items stay in the inbox.' inbox.drain writes the catalog and deletes the accepted files before the render and check. When either of those fails, or an accepted file cannot be deleted, it raises `inbox: added <ids>, then: <reason>` (inbox.py:286-295) and the driver prints that as a `problem:` line with exit 2. The items are then already in the catalog and their inbox files are gone. A second case: when the todo-watch mod's drain holds the write lock for more than the 10 s wait, the skill's fallback drain refuses with a lock holder named `todo_sync.py add --inbox`, while the mod's drain is in fact adding those items. In both cases the relayed text tells the developer the items are still queued, which invites a manual re-add. A re-added `note` item has no issue number to dedupe on, so it would land twice.

Also (docs): Both skills say a `problem:` line from `add --inbox` leaves 'the queued items ... in the inbox'. inbox.drain writes the catalog and deletes the accepted files before the render and check (inbox.py:286-288), and a later render, check or report failure raises `inbox: added <ids>, then: <error>` (inbox.py:290-295): those items are in the catalog and gone from the inbox. The session told they are still queued may report them as not added.

Also (skill_package): add-todo Step 4 (lines 85-86) and sync-gh-todo Step 3 (lines 75-76) say: 'A `problem:` line ends the run: relay it once without rerunning the drain; the queued items stay in the inbox.' The driver contradicts that in two cases. (1) inbox.drain (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:286-295) writes the catalog and deletes the accepted files before the render/check follow-up; a follow-up failure raises `inbox: added <ids>, then: <reason>`, so the items already landed and their files are gone, and _problems (inbox.py:227-228) can also report landed files that could not be deleted and must be removed by hand before the next drain. (2) When the todo-watch mod's own drain (up to 60 s, plugins/todo-watch/hooks/inbox.ts:19) still holds the lock past the 10 s wait (todo_sync.py:110-111), the skill's drain refuses with a lock-held `problem:` naming `todo_sync.py add --inbox` as owner while that mod drain is landing the items. In both cases the session is told to report the items as still queued when they are, or are about to be, in the catalog.

Also (overall): The add-todo and sync-gh-todo drain steps say a `problem:` line ends the run 'without rerunning the drain; the queued items stay in the inbox'. When the todo-watch mod's drain outlasts the Agent hook's wait cap, the skill's `add --inbox` finds the files still listed, waits 10 s on the lock and refuses with `lock ... held by 'todo_sync.py add --inbox'`. In that case the items are being added, not left queued, and the mod's summary line arrives as context later. The relayed message tells the developer the opposite.
fix: Reword both skill paragraphs: a `problem:` line that opens with `inbox: added` means those ids landed and only the render, check or file cleanup failed; a lock refusal naming `todo_sync.py add --inbox` means another drain (the todo-watch mod) holds the lock and the items arrive through its summary line; any other `problem:` line leaves the queued items in the inbox.

Replace the sentence in both skills with: 'A `problem:` line ends the run: relay it once without rerunning the drain. When it opens with `inbox: added`, those items landed and only the render or check failed; otherwise the queued items stay in the inbox.'

In both skills replace the closing sentence with: 'A `problem:` line ends the run: relay it once without rerunning the drain. When it opens with `inbox: added`, those items landed and only the follow-up failed; when it names a lock held by `todo_sync.py add --inbox`, the todo-watch mod is draining and its summary line arrives as context; otherwise the queued items stay in the inbox.'

Add one sentence to both drain steps: a `problem:` line naming the holder `todo_sync.py add --inbox` means the todo-watch drain is still running; its summary line arrives as context and nothing needs rerunning.

Add a `scratch_folder` | `docs/_scratch/` | `<scratch_folder>/todo-inbox` (inbox the drain lists) row to the config table. Add hook-table rows for `tool.call` on Agent (a completed harness:todo-editor drains and appends the summary), subagent `turn.complete` (drain when an item is queued) and `session.start` (drain left-over items). Update plugins/todo-watch/README.md: reword lines 9-10 (the mod also runs the harness inbox drain, never writing the catalog itself); add a `scratch_folder` row (`docs/_scratch/`, the inbox folder `<scratch_folder>/todo-inbox` it lists); add Hooks rows for `tool.call` on `Agent` (foreground todo-editor result drains and appends the summary), `turn.complete` for subagent loops (drain when the inbox lists a queued file) and the session.start drain; add a behavior rule or a 'Inbox drains' subsection under Check runs giving the `add --inbox` argv, the 60 s DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS, the single-flight-plus-one-owed pacing and how a pending summary reaches a tool result or prompt.
Extend the README.md:41 todo-watch row's notes with one bullet: drains the TODO inbox when a todo-editor agent returns.

Add a short section to plugins/todo-watch/README.md on the inbox drain (triggers, the single-flight run, the `inbox:` context line, `scratch_folder`), and one bullet to the todo-watch row in README.md:41.

important.name: Unreadable-lock and break-guard paths untested
important.summary: The test module's docstring (line 6) says an unreadable lock goes stale 'when older than WRITE_STALE_SECONDS', but no test plants an unreadable body. That leaves _is_stale(body None) and _unlink_if_same(observed None) with no coverage. The <lock>.break guard is not covered either: a busy guard should make break_if_unchanged return False by the deadline or raise LockError without one, and a guard older than WAIT_SECONDS should be cleared only while its token is unchanged. The catalog_lock module docstring presents these as the race protections, yet a regression in any of them (for example a half-written lock that never goes stale and blocks every writer) would pass the suite.
fix: Add tests that: write a non-JSON lock body, check that hold refuses while its mtime is fresh, then backdate it past WRITE_STALE_SECONDS with os.utime and check that hold breaks it; plant a fresh '<lock>.break' guard and assert break_if_unchanged(path, body, deadline=time.monotonic()) is False and that a call without a deadline raises LockError (with WAIT_SECONDS patched small); backdate the guard past WAIT_SECONDS and assert the break succeeds.

important.name: Spec-order sort test cannot catch a lost zero pad
important.summary:
test_put_names_sort_in_spec_order_on_a_repeated_stamp queues six items, so the indices are 0..5. inbox._write_items zero-pads the index (width = max(2, len(str(len(items) - 1)))) so names still sort in spec order past index 9. Unpadded single digits sort the same way, so the test passes even if the padding is removed. It only fails if the index is dropped altogether. A regression in the padding would let a drain of a 10+ item put land items out of spec order, and no test would catch it.

Also (tests): The put docstring promises 'A put is all or nothing: a failed inbox write leaves nothing queued'. _write_items deletes every hidden or renamed file written so far when a later write fails. The only failure test, test_a_failed_inbox_write_names_the_issue_already_filed, makes write_atomic refuse on the first call, so nothing has been written yet. It checks only the error text and never asserts that the inbox is empty. The cleanup loop, and the failure of a rename after the first file has gone visible, have no coverage.

Also (adv_code_tests): The put docstring promises that a failed inbox write leaves nothing queued, and _write_items enforces that by deleting every file written so far (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:109-113). No test reaches that path with a file already on disk. test_a_failed_inbox_write_names_the_issue_already_filed fails the first write_atomic, so nothing exists to clean up, and it never asserts that the inbox is empty. If the cleanup were removed, a rename that fails on the second item would leave the first item queued while put reports failure. A retried put would then queue that item twice, and a local note would land in the catalog twice.

Attack: Replace inbox._write_items with a copy that omits the try/except cleanup (inbox.py:102-113). All five put tests in tests/lib/test_todo_sync_inbox.py still pass. Then, with report._replace_with_retry raising OSError on call 4, inbox.put(cfg, spec of _item(9), _item(12)) raises while inbox.queued(cfg) lists one file that the next drain adds. The same failure against the real code leaves the folder empty. Run as probes/test_cleanup_probe.py, 7 passed.
fix: Queue at least 11 items (for example issues 9 and 12..21) so that index 10 must sort after index 2. Keep the existing assertions that the sorted names equal result.paths and that the issues come back in spec order.
Add a test that patches inbox.write_atomic to succeed once and then raise OSError on a two-item spec. Assert that put raises and that `_names(cfg) == []`.
Add a second case where `inbox._report._replace_with_retry` fails on the second rename, and assert that the first renamed file is gone too. Also assert the empty inbox in the existing #42 test.

Add a test that patches report._replace_with_retry to raise OSError on its 4th call (two hidden writes, then the second rename) during a two-item put, then asserts pytest.raises(OSError) and that inbox_dir holds no file.
Extend test_a_failed_inbox_write_names_the_issue_already_filed so the second write fails, and assert that the inbox folder is empty afterwards.

important.name: Drain failure branches have no tests
important.summary: drain's docstring lists several failure behaviors. (1) A catalog that cannot be ranked raises and leaves the inbox untouched (_probe). (2) Accepted files that cannot be deleted are named to be deleted before the next drain (_remove_accepted / _problems). (3) Refused files that cannot be set aside are reported and refused again next time (_set_aside_all). (4) When items landed, the message opens with the ids added. Only the render-failure path is tested (test_a_failed_render_after_the_write_never_adds_the_items_twice). A regression in _probe would set every queued file aside as rejected because of a catalog-level fault, and no test would see it.
fix: Add tests that: corrupt the catalog ranking so drain raises 'catalog cannot be ranked' and the queued files are still there; patch inbox._unlink_with_retry to raise OSError and assert the error names the file and opens with 'inbox: added'; patch inbox._set_aside to raise OSError and assert the 'could not be set aside' sentence.

The TASK-6 receipt lists no extra files, but band.test.tsx and summary.test.ts changed. The gh.py timeout (GH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) belongs to no plan task. DesignEvolution.json records only EX1, so a reader of the plan cannot tell these deviations were intended.

Also (system_shape): Plan TASK-6 (ActionPlan.json:343) specifies three behaviors. (b) A backgrounded todo-editor's `async_launched` agentId is recorded, and only that agent's `turn.complete` starts a drain. (c) A task-notification prompt waits up to DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS. (d) The session-start drain lists the inbox. The build differs on two counts. It records no agentId and drains at any subagent's turn end whenever the inbox lists a queued file (checks.ts:645-656, drainQueued at 591). It caps every wait at the hook budget less 1 s (`waitCapMs`, inbox.ts:64-67). The `gh` call timeout (gh.py GH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, commits 41d3ec0/7168893) lies outside every TASK's file list. DesignEvolution.json holds only EX1 (the state_dir skip), so the plan, the spec's Decided 17 and the code now tell three different stories about when the mod drains.
fix: Add DesignEvolution entries (through the plan driver) for the broadened turn.complete trigger, the todo-watch test adaptations and the gh call timeout, and re-record the TASK-6 receipt with its extra files.

Add DesignEvolution entries (EX2 for the any-subagent turn-end trigger and the budget-capped wait, EX3 for the `gh` timeout) through the plan driver, so the PIP's Design changes section explains the deviation; leave the frozen spec as written.

minor.name: _write_items says a drain never sees part of a put, but the renames are sequential
minor.summary:
inbox._write_items (inbox.py:92-96) says 'so a drain never sees part of a put', and put (inbox.py:120-121) promises 'a failed inbox write leaves nothing queued'. The hidden-then-rename step only keeps a half-written file out of view. The renames at inbox.py:106-108 run one by one, so a concurrent drain (any subagent turn end in the mod) can list and absorb the first k items before rename k+1. If a later rename fails, the rollback deletes files that are already gone, and put raises as if nothing was queued while k items are in the catalog. A rerun of the put then duplicates them.

Also (overall): inbox.py:95-96 says each item is written under a hidden name and renamed afterwards "so a drain never sees part of a put". The renames run one at a time (lines 106-108), so a drain that lists the folder between two renames sees only some of the put's files. A todo-watch drain triggered by any other subagent's turn end can run at that moment. If a later rename then fails, the cleanup at lines 109-113 unlinks files that drain already added to the catalog and the put reports failure, so the agent's rerun queues duplicates. Hiding the files only protects against a half-written file, not against a partial put.
fix: Reword both docstrings to the guarantee that holds: a drain never reads a half-written file, and a put that fails during the renames may already have had its earlier items drained.
Or give the hidden files one put-id prefix and rename them under the catalog lock, so a drain sees all of a put or none of it.
Reword the docstring: hidden names keep a drain from reading a half-written file, but a drain may take the renamed files of a put whose later renames are still pending.

Or make the put visible at once: write all items to a hidden staging subfolder and rename that folder's contents only after a marker, or have queued() ignore a stamp group until a `<stamp>.done` marker exists.

minor.name: locking._verify duplicates catalog_lock._check_lease
minor.summary:
locking._verify (locking.py:68-74) repeats the body read, the mode check, the token check and the error wording of catalog_lock._check_lease (catalog_lock.py:333-341). The two copies can drift. release then runs the same check a second time through free -> release_lease.

Also (overall): locking.py:68-74 reads the holder and refuses on 'no lease' or 'carries another token' with the same logic and nearly the same messages as catalog_lock._check_lease (catalog_lock.py:333-341). The two copies can drift, for example if one is later changed to treat a stale lease as no lease.
fix: Make _check_lease public (check_lease) and have _verify call it inside try/except catalog_lock.LockError -> TodoSyncError, as free does.
Expose the check from catalog_lock (rename `_check_lease` to `check_lease`) and have locking.release call it inside a `try/except catalog_lock.LockError -> TodoSyncError`, then delete `_verify`.

minor.name: migrate-ids and init take no --lease, so a lease holder cannot run them
minor.summary:
The docstring says every catalog write without --lease TOKEN waits and then refuses while a lease is held, and gives retire, split, refresh and add a --lease option. init (GUARDED, plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.py dispatch) and migrate-ids (locking.leased takes its own lease) get none, so the owner of an acquired lease cannot run either until it releases.

Attack: In a project with todo.folder set: run 'todo_sync.py lease acquire --owner batch' (prints 'lease: <token>'), then 'todo_sync.py migrate-ids --lease <token>' fails at argparse (unrecognized arguments), and 'todo_sync.py migrate-ids' waits 10 s and exits 2 with 'problem: lock ... is held by 'batch' (lease, ...)'. Same for 'todo_sync.py init --lease <token>'.
fix: Add --lease TOKEN to init and migrate-ids; pass it to locking.guard for init and make locking.leased run under the given lease (no acquire or free) when a token is passed.
Or state in the todo_sync.py docstring that init and migrate-ids refuse while any lease is held and must run outside a lease.

minor.name: add-todo rule 'the main session does not write the catalog' now sits beside a main-session catalog write

The Rules bullet at line 104 still reads 'The main session does not write the catalog. Not one entry, not "just this once"'. The intent (the session never authors entries; ids, ranks and counts belong to todo_sync.py) still holds, but read literally the rule forbids the step the skill now requires, and a session following the rule strictly could skip the drain when the todo-watch mod is not installed, leaving the item queued.
fix: Reword line 104 to: '**The main session does not edit the catalog.** Not one entry, not "just this once": the Step 4 drain is its only catalog write, and ids, ranks and counts belong to `todo_sync.py`, the drafting to the agent.'

minor.name: Drain's hidden-file skip is never exercised in Python
minor.summary:
put writes each item under a hidden '.<final>.json' name and then renames it (inbox._hidden, _write_items). inbox.queued skips such files with `not p.name.startswith('.')`. test_drain_skips_temp_and_rejected_files only plants '.20261113T000001Z-aaaaaa.json.x1.tmp'. That name already fails the `.endswith('.json')` filter, so deleting the hidden-name clause leaves every Python test green. A drain could then absorb a put that is still in progress, and the put's later rename would fail after the items had landed. The TS side does pin the case (isQueuedName with a hidden .json), but nothing pins the driver that actually drains.

Also (adv_code_tests): test_drain_skips_temp_and_rejected_files plants '.20261113T000001Z-aaaaaa.json.x1.tmp', which queued() already drops for not ending in '.json'. The hidden name _write_items really writes ('.<stamp>-NN-<hex>.json') ends in '.json', so the leading-dot filter at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:149, the guard that keeps a drain from picking up a put that is still in progress, has no Python test. The TS isQueuedName test does cover the dotted .json name; the Python side does not.

Attack: Monkeypatch inbox.queued with a copy that drops `and not p.name.startswith(".")` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:149) and call test_drain_skips_temp_and_rejected_files: it still passes. With the same patch, a drain over an inbox holding only '.20261113T000001000000Z-00-aaaaaa.json' adds issue #9. Both were run as probes (probes/test_hidden_probe.py, 2 passed).
fix: In test_drain_skips_temp_and_rejected_files, also queue a hidden '.20261113T000001Z-01-aaaaaa.json' (the name put actually leaves) and keep the assertion that nothing is added or rejected.
Alternatively, add a direct `inbox.queued(cfg)` assertion covering the hidden .json, the .tmp and the .rejected.json names.

Add a planted file named like a real hidden put, e.g. _queue(cfg, '.20261113T000001000000Z-00-aaaaaa.json', [_item(9)]), to test_drain_skips_temp_and_rejected_files, and keep the existing .tmp file alongside it.
